title: 🗄️ Data Model
help: A live, introspected map of everything AgentCase actually holds — not a diagram somebody drew once and forgot to update, but four tables each read directly off the running registries at the moment you open them. If a field is added, renamed or removed in the code, this page reflects it on the next reload with
. That is the whole design point: a data-model page that can drift from the code is worse than no page at all, because it teaches the wrong thing with total confidence.

🔍 Why four separate tables, not one
These are genuinely different kinds of data with different failure modes. A
can be deleted and the menu simply loses a tab. A
missing from the registry is a silent data-loss bug — the field looks fine until the user reloads. A
is read-only and derived, so it can never itself be wrong, only mis-bound. A

is a literal embedded in a formula, and the entire "tier 1/2/3 audit" work earlier in this build existed because those used to be invisible. Collapsing them into one table would hide exactly the distinction that makes each one worth checking.
